Third Quarter 2026 and Recent Highlights (Unless otherwise stated, all percentage changes represent year-over-year comparisons and do not exclude the prior-period results of Ketjen’s refining catalyst solutions business in which the company sold a 51% stake on March 2, 2026) • Net sales of $1.6 billion, up 19% due to higher pricing in Energy Storage (+68%) and higher pricing and volumes in Specialties (price +10%, volume +3%). • Net income of $297 million, or $2.15 per diluted share attributable to common shareholders; Adjusted net income (a) of $354 million, or $2.58 per diluted share attributable to common shareholders which primarily excludes restructuring and other related charges. • Adjusted EBITDA (a) of $646 million; up 186% due primarily to higher pricing in Energy Storage, increased pricing and volumes in Specialties and cost and productivity improvements. • Cash from operating activities of $406 million and free cash flow of $325 million (a) . Operating cash flow conversion of 63% (a) , supported by a cash dividend from the Talison joint venture which partly offset timing of working capital changes. • Delivered more than $150 million in year-to-date run -rate cost and productivity improvements, achieving the high end of our full-year target . • Talison’s Chemical Grade Plant 3 (CGP3) achieved 30-days of nameplate performance in September. • Improving full-year 2026 outlook considerations including: ◦ Specialties adjusted EBITDA of $350-$375 million (up from $275-$325 million), in part driven by ongoing cost and productivity improvements. ◦ Reducing full-year capital expenditure forecast to $300-$350 million (down from approximately $500 million), reflecting continued benefits from our focused capital efficiency improvements, as well as resequencing of some early-stage projects. (a) See Non-GAAP Reconciliations for further details. “Albemarle delivered another solid quarter, reflecting disciplined execution across the enterprise,” said Kent Masters, Chairman and CEO. “In Specialties, improved pricing and sustained progress on cost and productivity initiatives support an additional increased outlook for the year. Global lithium demand is up 48% year-to-date though August, driven by both electric vehicles and energy storage, reinforcing our confidence in the long-term outlook for the industry. We will continue to prioritize high-return organic growth by leveraging our advantaged resource base, capital spending efficiency, and financial flexibility.” 1 Third Quarter 2026 Results In millions, except per share amounts Q3 2026 Q3 2025 Change % Change Net sales $ 1,553.1 $ 1,307.8 $ 245.3 18.8 % Net income (loss) attributable to Albemarle Corporation $ 296.8 $ (160.7) $ 457.4 NM Adjusted EBITDA (a) $ 645.5 $ 225.6 $ 419.9 186.1 % Diluted income (loss) per share attributable to common shareholders $ 2.15 $ (1.72) $ 3.87 NM Non-operating pension and OPEB items (a) 0.01 — Non-recurring and other unusual items (a) 0.41 1.53 Adjusted diluted income (loss) per share attributable to common shareholders (a)(b) $ 2.58 $ (0.19) $ 2.77 NM (a) See Non-GAAP Reconciliations for further details. Net sales for the third quarter of 2026 were $1.6 billion, up 19%, driven primarily by higher prices in both Energy Storage and Specialties and volume growth in Specialties. Adjusted EBITDA of $646 million increased by $420 million from the prior-year quarter, primarily due to higher net sales and ongoing cost and productivity improvements. Net income attributable to Albemarle of $297 million increased year over year by $457 million. The effective income tax rate for the third quarter of 2026 was 16.4% or 5.8% on an adjusted basis due to geographic income mix. Energy Storage net sales for the third quarter of 2026 were $1.1 billion, an increase of $410 million, or 58%, due to higher pricing. Adjusted EBITDA of $560 million increased $436 million, or 351%, primarily due to improved lithium pricing and partially offset by higher price spodumene inventory processed in the quarter and increased Chilean commissions. Sales volume declined year-over-year primarily due to timing events in the prior-year period, including inventory destocking and higher-than-usual spodumene shipments, which led to the third quarter of 2025 being the segment’s record highest volume quarter on a lithium carbonate equivalent (LCE) basis. Specialties Results In millions Q3 2026 Q3 2025 Change % Change Net Sales $ 388.6 $ 345.0 $ 43.7 12.7 % Adjusted EBITDA $ 98.7 $ 75.5 $ 23.2 30.7 % Specialties net sales for the third quarter of 2026 were $389 million, an increase of $44 million, or 13%, primarily due to higher pricing (+10%) and volumes (+3%). Adjusted EBITDA of $99 million increased $23 million, or 31%, primarily due to higher volumes and favorable pricing in bromine and derivatives, along with continued productivity improvements and proactive management of cost escalations driven by the conflict in the Middle East. Additionally, the Jordan Bromine Company (JBC) joint venture achieved record quarterly production. 2026 Outlook Considerations Total Corporate Outlook Considerations The table below reflects expected outcomes for the total company based on recently observed lithium market price scenarios. Outlook ranges for each scenario are based on variation in sales volume and product mix. Energy Storage production volumes are expected to increase year over year. Sales volumes are expected to be in the range of 225 to 235 kilotons lithium carbonate equivalent, as increased Wodgina volumes partially offset a 2 delay in the Talison CGP3 ramp due to a fire that occurred on June 9. All three scenarios assume flat market pricing flowing through Energy Storage’s current contract book which includes approximately 40% of salts volume (or one-third of total volumes) on long-term agreements. Scenarios also assume that spodumene pricing averages 10% of the lithium carbonate equivalent (LCE) price, while other costs are assumed to be constant. Specialties Outlook Considerations Specialties adjusted EBITDA outlook is improved as strong year-to-date performance, primarily driven by cost and productivity improvements, more than offset supply chain related cost escalation due to the conflict in the Middle East. Our outlook continues to reflect modest volume growth in key end markets led by semiconductors, oil and gas, fl ame retardants and pharmaceuticals and steady year-to-date demand in automotive and petrochemical markets. Fourth quarter outlook assumes steady demand in the bromine market and the impact of the ongoing situation in the Middle East. About Albemarle Albemarle Corporation (NYSE: ALB) is a world leader in transforming essential resources into critical ingredients for mobility, energy, connectivity and health. We partner to pioneer new ways to move, power, connect and protect with people and planet in mind. A reliable and high-quality global supply of lithium and bromine allows us to deliver advanced solutions for our customers. Learn more about how the people of Albemarle are enabling a more resilient world at Albemarle.com.
